story_type: Mercury capsule low on fuel, late retrofire, overshoots and is found at sea, NASA TV film
hook: He splashed down off target. Finding him took 45 minutes.
narration: He came down far off target, and it took forty five minutes to find him.
1962. Scott Carpenter rode Aurora 7 into orbit, the second American to circle the Earth.
Soon the horizon scanner, the sensor that keeps the capsule lined up with the planet, malfunctioned.
His fuel for steering ran down faster than the ground expected.
The cabin heated up, and sweat got into his eyes.
Then the timer for his retro rockets failed. He had to fire them by hand.
At five miles per second, every three seconds of delay puts you fifteen miles further down range.
Coming back in, he spent the last of his fuel steering, and the capsule swung through almost a full circle.
[short pause] He popped the drogue chute early, at twenty six thousand feet, and the swinging came under control.
Gus Grissom radioed that he had overshot, and recovery teams were on their way.
About forty five minutes after splashdown, planes from the carrier Intrepid spotted him.
outcome: Rescue swimmers jumped in to secure the capsule, and Scott Carpenter arrived safely aboard Intrepid.
title: Overshot his landing, found 45 min later
description:
In May 1962, Mercury astronaut Scott Carpenter flew Aurora 7 with a failed horizon scanner, falling fuel and a retro rocket timer that would not fire, then came down beyond his target. Planes from the USS Intrepid found him about 45 minutes after splashdown. From the NASA Television tribute Mission: Aurora 7, which uses NASA mission footage.
